instrument.state: An internal structure cannot be sampled directly, but variations within it systematically alter the propagation of signals that cross it along many paths.
instrument.operation: Measure signal travel behavior across many source-to-receiver paths, compare those observations with predictions from a candidate internal model, and iteratively adjust the model to reduce the discrepancies.
instrument.signal: The observed propagation times or waveforms differ from model predictions in spatially structured ways across the sampled paths.
instrument.inference: The pattern of discrepancies constrains a spatial model of internal properties that could have produced the observed propagation behavior.
instrument.limit: Sparse or uneven path coverage, measurement error, uncertain source locations, regularization choices, model assumptions, and non-uniqueness can create artifacts or allow multiple internal structures to fit the observations.

target.question: Which release-workflow dependencies account for intermittent publication failures, and what bounded remedy is supported?
evidence: Authored synthetic scenario; no claim about a real organization or person.

A controlled release emulator exposes end-to-end artifact transit times over many known overlapping dependency paths. Internal job timestamps are withheld. Repeated trials with injected stage delays validate an additive timing model in the emulator; delayed arrival triggers the reproducible publication timeout.

mapping.state: Hidden per-stage transit delays affect observed end-to-end propagation along release paths.
mapping.operation: Send equivalent artifacts across known paths, compare measured times with a candidate internal stage-delay map, and iteratively invert structured residuals to refine the map and test held-out routes.
mapping.signal: Path-specific time discrepancies identify combinations of hidden delays compatible with timeouts.
mapping.inference: Constrain an internal delay map and candidate dependency remedies for the timeout within the emulator.
mapping.limit: Sparse coverage, measurement noise, model assumptions, regularization and non-unique maps limit causal specificity and live-system generalization.
